common_name: Admiral Amazon African Violet (Large Standard Lavender-Flowered Cultivar)

planting.note: Root leaf-stem cuttings in moistened propagating mix year-round as a houseplant; new plantlets emerge from the petiole base in 4-8 weeks.

directions: Root leaf cuttings in moist propagating mix and grow as a houseplant in bright indirect light, never direct sun, in slightly acidic, well-drained potting mix. Admiral Amazon is a Large Standard cultivar registered in 1942 by the pioneering California hybridizing house Armacost & Royston, bearing single lavender flowers over broad, quilted 'Supreme'-type foliage that grows notably larger than many older African violet selections. Keep water off the crown and leaves when irrigating, feed lightly every three to four weeks during active growth, and divide or refresh crowded crowns from leaf cuttings as older plants decline. Its larger leaf spread means it benefits from a slightly roomier pot than standard-sized violets.

common_name: Dark Mambo Rex Begonia (Near-Black Velvety Rippled Foliage)

planting.note: Grow year-round as a houseplant in bright, indirect light; if summering outdoors keep in deep, sheltered shade and bring back indoors before nights drop toward 55F.

directions: Pot in a light, fast-draining, humus-rich mix and grow in bright, filtered light with no direct sun, which scorches the thin leaf surface. Dark Mambo, also sold as Black Mambo, is a modern Rex begonia cultivar with near-black, velvety, rippled leaves carrying subtle burgundy undertones across the rumpled surface, the dark blades held above conspicuously pale, contrasting petioles. Keep humidity elevated with a pebble tray or by grouping with other foliage plants, and let the topsoil dry slightly between waterings to prevent rhizome rot, since Rex begonias are grown chiefly for foliage and the small flowers are often removed. Propagate by rhizome division or leaf-wedge cuttings taken at repotting time.

common_name: Amazon Mist New Zealand Hair Sedge

planting.note: Set out divisions or container plants in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; sharp winter drainage matters more to this sedge's survival than cold air temperatures.

directions: Amazon Mist forms a fine-textured, arching tussock of hair-like silvery sage-green foliage that gives the clump a soft, misty appearance distinct from the bronze and near-white tones of its Carex comans siblings. Slender brown flower spikes rise on wiry stems above the foliage in mid to late summer, adding subtle seasonal interest without detracting from the plant's main appeal as a texture and color accent. It performs best in full sun to light shade with consistently moist, well-drained soil, and makes an effective edging, container, or small-scale groundcover plant where its soft, cascading mound can be appreciated up close. Comb out dead blades by hand in early spring rather than shearing, and divide congested clumps every few years to keep the color and texture fresh.
